reviews.review: I enjoy cozy games, and this is a cozy game. But I wouldn't recommend it. Its uneventful and it has similar vibes of animal crossing, but the story is boring and I lost interest in a few hours. I haven't played the game again since and have no desire to do so. There are much better simulation games on the market, with better play. Sorry Devs. It has some cute aspects, but honestly, I would never recommend this game unless it was at a VERY deep discount, or in a game bundle pack with other games you want to play.

Just feels very empty. The villagers have no souls, like dolls moving without purpose as they stare about, like a cheap version of animal crossing. Sorry Devs.

I've tried a lot to really enjoy this game but I just can't... There just feels like it's missing so much. The gameplay is so slow and unrewarding and there's no sense of direction. The game's way too zoomed in but that just shows how small the game world actually is, and how little there is to do. The farming portion of the game is obnoxious, being able to water 1 plant at a time and only 6 plants before you have to refill your watering can. 

I don't know, maybe I'm just not getting it, but I can't see how this hasn't been polished and added to over the years its been out, it definitely isn't finished
Just do not buy it if you are 8+ years old

I wanted to like it, I truly did. This isn't the cozy, Animal Crossing like I was promised. I didn't expect it to be on par with one of Nintendo's best franchises but it just fails to deliver on everything. None of the animals are interesting to talk to beyond 3 sentences, there's little to do after the early game besides grind, the exploration is minimal. The ONLY okay thing is the customization mechanics but they are buggy to work with and the placement boxes are wonky. It's a pretty game, that's it. 

It would be okay if it was early access but the devs say THIS is the complete game? Seriously? I'd be embarrassed if my creative project came out like this and the devs should be too. It's clear it's made to suck you in for 2 hours so you cannot refund it.

Trust me, I tried to love it after a certain YT video sung its praises. I tried to tell myself it would get better or I'm placing too high of expectations on it but it's clear after I bought it from early access years ago this opinion won't change. Please do not buy this, there are so many better cozy games out there from other indie devs. Try Spiritfarer or Stardew Valley instead.

It gets veeery grindy towards the end - at least if you`re going for all the Mayor Merits (sorta like ingame achievements/challenges which get you rewards and unlocks). I eventually gave up on that and settled for getting all Steam Achievements.
Aside from that, some things are a bit... wonky. I unlocked the weather control device before the sprinklers, making the latter pointless. If you use fertilizer to make higher quality veggies, these do not count for the all veggies achievement - only the regular ones do. The rewards you get for completing villager errands (usually clothes) seem to come from a very limited pool - I kept getting the same things over and over.

That being said I got the game on sale for 4 bucks. For that price it isn`t terrible... but not good either.

I was hoping to prove the negative reviews wrong but it's veryyyy slow and basically no gameplay, I ended up just sleeping through days to skip until there was something to do. The fact that you cant unlock certain things (like the map??) until you've sprinted for X amount of time is bonkers when your (invisible!) stamina bar drains in about 0.3 seconds. Pretty broken that you can steal everyones furniture from their house/shop and sell it with zero consequences, however, unfortunately this animal crossing knock off missed the mark :(

Despite the hours I've put into this, I struggle to play it. The game is relatively empty. There's no museum to complete. I liked the custom furniture mechanic. I want to 100% the achievements but every time I go into the game, no matter what I do, it feels like a chore. Farming feels horrendous when you first unlock it simply because your watering can can only water 6 crops until you have to refill it again. I'm sure there's an upgraded watering can, but it really shouldn't feel this bad when you're just starting. 

I struggle to find the purpose of playing this game. Animal Crossing has many sets to collect, furniture wise and clothing wise. But in this game it forces you to rely on your own creations or other players creations when it comes to decorating. Many of the items you can buy are lackluster, and aren't all that appealing. Which can suck if you're not really that good with the customization features.

The merits update is what brought me back at one point hence the hours, but I haven't gotten all of them yet. While the merits give me things to do and rewards for doing them, there's A LOT of requirements needed. Most of which can be gotten over time, but if you struggle with the customization features, and dislike the farming, it's a lot more difficult to get through the merits that requires those two things.

For anything that requires me to have a certain amount of custom creations, it's a lot easier if I just place one piece down on a decoration blueprint, save, and repeat until I reach the needed amount. But doing it that way simply just defeats the purpose of having the custom creation features. I don't have fun spending HOURS on ONE DECENT blueprint just to see that I'm not making ANY progress in getting the merits that require me to have multiple custom creations. It's a quantity over quality issue for me. Don't get me wrong, I love making my own furniture, especially when it comes to making my own storage solutions. But it isn't reasonable to put in actual effort into making blueprints/clothes if some merits requires wayyyyy too much, as it would take WAYYYYYY too many hours just to get one merit done.

Now I don't want to discourage the dev that worked on this game. But I just feel like this game had way too much wasted potential, and the game comes off to people as an Animal Crossing rip-off. Even more so because the dev just stopped doing anything with the game all together. Whether that's due to lack of funding or not. I mean they stopped updating New Horizons but even that game has way more in terms of content, and that game forces you to play every day due to how time-gated that game is. And after playing this game, I'm starting to understand why the Animal Crossing series as a whole is time-gated.

I really tried to give this game a chance but I just found no real purpose or enjoyment from it. I've over 150 hours on ACNH and many hours playing cosy games so I do enjoy laid back cosy games. However, for me this game is, sadly, bland and empty feeling.

Hokko Life: A Relaxing Escape That Falls Short of Its Competition

Hokko Life is a charming attempt to join the ranks of life-sim and farming games, but it struggles to stand out in a genre filled with stronger contenders. While it offers a peaceful, laid-back experience, it lacks the depth and polish needed to compete with its more advanced peers like Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing.

At its core, Hokko Life is a game about creativity and relaxation. The customization options for designing furniture and decorating your town are a highlight, giving players freedom to express themselves. However, beyond this, the game quickly becomes repetitive and feels surprisingly empty. The farming mechanics are basic, the character interactions lack personality, and progression feels slow and uninspired compared to other games in the genre.

If you’re looking for a very chill game with no pressure or urgency, Hokko Life might suit you. It’s pleasant and easygoing, making it a decent pick for those who want a simple, stress-free escape. But for anyone looking for a more engaging or rewarding experience, it has little to offer. The gameplay never feels innovative, and the lack of meaningful features leaves the game feeling like an undercooked version of its competitors.

Pros:
	•	Relaxing, stress-free gameplay
	•	Nice creative tools for furniture and town design

Cons:
	•	Lacks depth and meaningful content
	•	Farming and interactions are underdeveloped
	•	Feels uninspired compared to stronger titles in the genre

Final Thoughts: Hokko Life is a pleasant distraction, but it doesn’t bring anything special to the table. If it wants to compete with its more advanced peers, it needs to try harder to offer something unique and memorable. For now, it’s a nice option for players who want a slower pace, but others will likely find themselves moving on quickly.
